hero.title: Agents forced
hero.lede: Dekopon is the pluggable, remixable, safe way to run your own AI agents. Models request actions and your dekopon gates everything. Agents can't even see credentials, everything is stored safely inside of dekopon.

visual.caption: The model requests an action. The broker grants permission and attaches the credential.

constitution.title: A change is judged by which goal it serves.
constitution.intro: Three goals, in priority order; a subsystem that serves none of them is a deletion candidate, however well built.

goals.title: Credentials are unleakable.
goals.body: A model may reference a secret; it cannot read any: secret bytes exist only inside the broker, and the native HTTP engine injects them after the component has built its request.

goals.title: One trace, complete.
goals.body: One W3C trace per message carries the whole run: every prompt, every command word with its arguments, every decision, every HTTP call.

goals.title: Extensible through Wasm providers.
goals.body: New capability arrives as an out-of-tree component with a manifest and command words, executed under exact owner-authored constraints; nothing in this tree grows to add one.

nonGoals.title: Six non-goals
nonGoals.note: An argument for keeping or adding code on any of these grounds is rejected on sight.
items: Idempotency, exactly-once, duplicate-effect defense, automatic retries
Crash durability, reconcilable state, audit tamper-detection
A compromised host, root, or a malicious process in the broker’s trust domain

useCases.title: Familiar tools, bounded access.
useCases.intro: Bash is built in; add Wasm providers for the jobs you want your agent to do. Start with the established tools, then explore the newer integrations.

items.label: bash
items.title: Bash-style workflows
items.body: Chain tools with structured pipelines, loops, and text processing. No OS shell or host filesystem.

items.label: gh
items.title: GitHub reviews and triage
items.body: Read pull requests and CI results; comment, review, or merge with separate grants.

items.label: ripgrep
items.title: Search supplied text
items.body: Use real ripgrep matching with context and precise locations. Documents are inputs, not host files.

items.label: python
items.title: Python for data work
items.body: Calculate and transform JSON or YAML in a fresh RustPython sandbox. No pip or host files.

items.label: curl
items.title: Fetch approved URLs
items.body: Read HTTPS pages and API responses through broker-controlled destinations and authentication.

items.label: gpt-image
items.title: Generate and remix images
items.body: Create a PNG from a prompt or reference photos using your ChatGPT subscription.

items.label: SQL · Turso
items.title: SQLite-compatible records
items.body: Query and store structured data in broker-managed storage. Oversized writes can leave a database unreadable.
items.detail: Early SQL support · not the SQLite engine

link.label: Build a provider with the Rust SDK

closing.title: Start with one capability
closing.body: One capability, one policy, one trace. Let the model explore the rest without handing it the host.

protocols.title: Your agent, in your chat.
protocols.intro: Slack leads with its native Agent experience. The same runtime also connects to Discord, WhatsApp, and Telegram.
protocols.note: History is configurable and held in memory. Image understanding needs a compatible model; generated PNG replies require an enabled provider route.
